# epanet-js scripting API

> Sandboxed JavaScript scripting for epanet-js, a browser-based water network modelling app built on the EPANET engine. A script reads the open network — assets, patterns, curves, controls, the pipe library, settings — queries it spatially and topologically, runs the app's own review checks, exports it as INP, and hands results back as the map selection, a zoom, console output and attached files. This version is read-only: scripts cannot edit the model or run a simulation. Experimental — names may change.

This is the complete surface a script sees. Everything below is injected into
the sandbox; nothing else exists.

## How a script runs

- **Globals:** `network`, `selection`, `map`, `console`, `ui`. There is no `fetch`, DOM, `require`/`import`, timers (`setTimeout`), `structuredClone` or network access.
- **Standard JavaScript works:** `Array`, `Map`, `Set`, `JSON`, `Math`, `Number`, `String`, template strings, destructuring, `async`/`await` (top-level `await` is allowed).
- **The sandbox is SES (hardened JavaScript).** `Date.now()`, `new Date()` with no arguments and `Math.random()` throw. `new Date(milliseconds)` and date arithmetic on given values work. Do not reach for the current time or randomness.
- **Scripts run top to bottom, once.** Every call is synchronous. The script's output — `selection.set`, `map.zoomTo`, `ui.attachFile` — is applied when the script ends successfully. If the script throws, the error is shown with its line number and none of that output is applied (console lines already printed stay visible).
- **Read-only.** Every value a script receives is frozen. Assigning to an asset field throws (`Cannot set property diameter … which has only a getter`). Lists a member returns directly (`network.pipes`, `selection.assets`, `network.findWithin(...)`, `network.findSubnetworks()`) are fresh arrays the script may sort or push into. Arrays inside a returned object or an asset (`network.trace(...).nodes`, `finding.assets`, `junction.links`, `pipe.vertices`) are frozen: copy them first (`[...zone.nodes].sort(...)`).
- **Units:** every number is in the **project's units**. `network.units` maps each quantity to its unit (`network.units.diameter === "mm"`, `network.units.length === "m"`, `network.units.flow === "l/s"`). A unit of `null` means the quantity is dimensionless or depends on the model (e.g. roughness).
- **Labels:** assets are addressed by **label**, the name shown in the app and written to INP files. Labels are unique, case-insensitively, within the node group (junctions, reservoirs, tanks), within the link group (pipes, pumps, valves) and within customer points. A node and a link may share a label.
- **Coordinates** are `[lng, lat]` positions; a bounding box is `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]`.
- **Inactive assets** (`asset.isActive === false`) are in the collections and lookups but are left out of the simulation, the INP and the review checks.

## 1. `network` — the model

### 1.1 Overview

| Member | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `network.name` | The project's name — use it for report titles and file names. |
| `network.project` | `{ name, fileName, source, isDemo, unitSystem, headlossFormula }`. `source` is `"project"`, `"inp"` or `"new"`; `fileName` may be `null`; `headlossFormula` is `"H-W"`, `"D-W"` or `"C-M"`. |
| `network.stats` | `{ junctions, reservoirs, tanks, pipes, pumps, valves, customerPoints, bounds }` — counts per type and the `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` extent (or `null`). |
| `network.units` | Quantity → unit for every value the API hands out (see the list below). |
| `network.simulation` | The simulation settings the next run would use (see below). |

Start the first script on an unfamiliar model with `console.log(network.stats)` and `console.log(network.units)`.

**Units keys:** `diameter` (pipes, valves), `tankDiameter` (tanks), `length`, `elevation`, `head`, `pressure`, `flow`, `velocity`, `headloss`, `unitHeadloss`, `baseDemand`, `directDemand`, `actualDemand`, `customerDemand`, `customerDemandPerDay`, `initialLevel`, `minLevel`, `maxLevel`, `level`, `minVolume`, `volume`, `tankArea`, `power`, `speed`, `efficiency`, `roughness`, `minorLoss`, `emitterCoefficient`, `mixingFraction`, `tcvSetting`, `averageKwPerFlowUnit`, `waterAge`, `waterTrace`, `chemicalConcentration`, `netFlow`, `actualHead`, `status`. Mind the mapping: a tank's `diameter` is in `units.tankDiameter`, a pipe's in `units.diameter`.

**`network.simulation`** fields, with unset hydraulic options already resolved to what EPANET uses: `version`, `duration`, `hydraulicTimestep`, `reportTimestep`, `patternTimestep`, `qualityTimestep`, `ruleTimestep` (seconds; the last two may be `null`), `globalDemandMultiplier`, `demandModel` (`"DDA"` or `"PDA"`), `minimumPressure`, `requiredPressure`, `pressureExponent`, `emitterExponent`, `backflowAllowed`, `trials`, `accuracy`, `unbalancedMode` (`"STOP"` or `"CONTINUE"`), `unbalancedExtraTrials`, `headError`, `flowChange`, `checkFreq`, `maxCheck`, `dampLimit`, `viscosity`, `specificGravity`, `quality` (`"none"`, `"chemical"`, `"age"`, `"trace"`), `qualityChemicalName`, `qualityMassUnit`, `qualityTraceNode` (a node label or `null`), `tolerance`, `diffusivity`, `reactionBulkOrder`, `reactionWallOrder`, `reactionTankOrder`, `reactionGlobalBulk`, `reactionGlobalWall`, `reactionLimitingPotential`, `reactionRoughnessCorrelation`, `reportEnergy`, `energyGlobalEfficiency`, `energyGlobalPrice`, `energyGlobalPattern` (a pattern label or `null`), `energyDemandCharge`, `statusReport`. Scripts cannot run a simulation or read results yet.

### 1.2 Collections and lookup

| Member | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `network.junctions`, `.reservoirs`, `.tanks`, `.pipes`, `.pumps`, `.valves` | Every asset of that type. |
| `network.nodes`, `network.links`, `network.assets` | Every node, every link, everything. |
| `network.customerPoints` | Every customer point. |
| `network.getNode(label)` | The junction, reservoir or tank with that label, or `null`. |
| `network.getLink(label)` | The pipe, pump or valve with that label, or `null`. |
| `network.get(label)` | The node or link with that label, or `null`. Throws `network.get("X") matches a node and a link; use getNode or getLink` when both exist — prefer `getNode`/`getLink`. |
| `network.getCustomerPoint(label)` | The customer point with that label, or `null`. Customer points are a separate label group: `getNode`/`getLink` never return one. |

Lookups return `null` rather than throwing. The same asset is always the same object: `network.pipes[0] === network.getLink(network.pipes[0].label)`.

### 1.3 Assets

Every asset is a read-only object of getters.

**Every asset:** `uid` (an internal number — never persist it), `label`, `type` (`"junction"`, `"reservoir"`, `"tank"`, `"pipe"`, `"pump"`, `"valve"`), `isNode`, `isLink`, `isActive`, `isSelected` (in the user's selection, or the script's after `selection.set`), `geometry` (a GeoJSON `Point` or `LineString`), `getCustom(name)` (a custom attribute's value by its name, or `null`).

**Every node:** `coordinates`, `elevation`, `initialQuality`, `chemicalSourceType` (`"concen"`, `"mass"`, `"flowpaced"`, `"setpoint"` or `null`), `chemicalSourceStrength`, `chemicalSourcePattern` (a pattern label or `null`), `links` (the connected links).

| Type | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `junction` | `emitterCoefficient`, `demands` (`[{ base, pattern? }]` — the demand categories; `pattern` is a label, absent when none), `baseDemand` (the sum of the categories' `base`), `customerPoints` (the customer points allocated to it). |
| `reservoir` | `head`, `headPattern` (label or `null`). Reservoirs have `elevation` too. |
| `tank` | `initialLevel`, `minLevel`, `maxLevel`, `diameter` (in `units.tankDiameter`), `minVolume`, `overflow`, `mixingModel` (`"mixed"`, `"2comp"`, `"fifo"`, `"lifo"`), `mixingFraction`, `bulkReactionCoeff`, `volumeCurve` (label or `null`). |

**Every link:** `startNode`, `endNode` (the node objects; positive flow runs start → end), `length` (the stored length, in `units.length`), `geometryLength` (the length measured along the drawn line, in `units.length`), `vertices` (the intermediate `[lng, lat]` points), `pointAt(distance)` (the `[lng, lat]` point that far along the line, in the project length unit).

| Type | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `pipe` | `diameter`, `roughness` (the pipe's own value, often `null`), `appliedRoughness` (what EPANET receives — the pipe's value, else the pipe library's for its material and age, else `null`), `roughnessSource` (`"pipe"`, `"library"` or `null`), `minorLoss`, `status` (`"open"`, `"closed"`, `"cv"`), `material`, `year`, `bulkReactionCoeff`, `wallReactionCoeff`, `customerPoints` (the customer points connected to it). |
| `pump` | `status` (`"on"`, `"off"`), `definitionType` (`"power"`, `"designPointCurve"`, `"standardCurve"`, `"curveId"`), `power`, `curvePoints` (`[{ flow, head }]` however the pump is defined, or `null`), `designPoint` (`{ flow, head }` when the pump has a single point, else `null`), `curve` (the library curve's label when `definitionType === "curveId"`, else `null`), `speed`, `speedPattern`, `efficiencyCurve`, `energyPrice`, `energyPricePattern` (labels or `null`), `control` (see below). |
| `valve` | `kind` (`"prv"`, `"psv"`, `"fcv"`, `"pbv"`, `"tcv"`, `"gpv"`, `"pcv"`), `setting`, `diameter`, `minorLoss`, `status` (`"active"`, `"open"`, `"closed"`), `curve` (label or `null`), `targetNode` (a PRV's remote set-point node, or `null`), `targetNodeOptions()` (see 1.6). |

`pipe.roughness` is not what the engine gets: read `appliedRoughness`, and `roughnessSource` for where it came from. When both are `null` the INP carries `MISSING`.

**`pump.control`** is the pump's structured control from the app, or `null`:
- `{ type: "timed-setting", steps: [{ time, status, setting }] }` — `time` in seconds.
- `{ type: "level-setting", tank, on: { level, setting }, off: { level } }` — `tank` is the tank object.
- `{ type: "variable-speed-pump", quantity, targetAsset, target, minSpeed, maxSpeed, laggedPumps, schedule: [{ time, target }], tankLevels: { tank, onLevel, offLevel } | null }` — `quantity` is `"pressure"`, `"level"` or `"flow"`.

**Customer points:** `uid`, `label`, `type` (`"customerPoint"`), `isSelected`, `coordinates`, `geometry`, `demands` (`[{ base, pattern? }]`), `demand` (the sum of `base`, in `units.customerDemand`), `isConnected`, `pipe` and `junction` (where it is allocated, or `null`), `snapPoint` (the `[lng, lat]` point on the pipe, or `null`), `getCustom(name)`. A disconnected point contributes no demand.

### 1.4 Libraries, controls and attributes

| Member | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `network.patterns` | `[{ label, type, multipliers }]` — `type` is `"demand"`, `"reservoirHead"`, `"pumpSpeed"`, `"qualitySourceStrength"` or `"energyPrice"`. |
| `network.getPattern(label)` | One pattern, or `null`. |
| `network.curves` | `[{ label, type, points: [{ x, y }] }]` — `type` is `"pump"`, `"efficiency"`, `"volume"`, `"valve"` or `"headloss"`. |
| `network.getCurve(label)` | One curve, or `null`. |
| `network.pipeMaterials` | The pipe library: `[{ label, entries: [{ age, roughness }] }]`. |
| `network.rawControls` | The `[CONTROLS]` lines as INP text, e.g. `"LINK PU1 CLOSED IF NODE T1 ABOVE 5"`. Filter them as strings. |
| `network.rawRules` | The `[RULES]` blocks as INP text. |
| `network.customAttributes(type)` | The custom attributes defined for `"junction"`, `"reservoir"`, `"tank"`, `"pipe"`, `"pump"`, `"valve"` or `"customerPoint"`: `[{ name, type }]` with `type` `"text"` or `"number"`. Read a value with `asset.getCustom(name)`. |
| `network.defaultAllocationRules` | The default customer point allocation rules for the project's units: `[{ maxDistance, maxDiameter }]`. |

The pumps' structured controls are on `pump.control`, not in `rawControls`. Read both before judging why a pump is off or a valve is closed.

### 1.5 Spatial queries and geometry

| Member | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `network.findWithin(area, { types }?)` | The assets inside `area`, which may be a GeoJSON `Polygon`, a `MultiPolygon`, a `Feature` of one, a `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` box or a ring of `[lng, lat]` positions. Polygons with holes are not supported. `types` is a list of asset types and `"customerPoint"`; the default is every asset type (no customer points). |
| `network.findNear(position, { radius, types? })` | The assets within `radius` of a `[lng, lat]` position, nearest first. `radius` is in the project length unit. `types` as for `findWithin`. |
| `network.geo.distance(a, b)` | The geodesic distance between two positions, in the project length unit. |
| `network.geo.length(line)` | The length of a line of positions, in the project length unit. |
| `network.geo.pointAlong(line, distance)` | The position that far along a line. |
| `network.geo.nearestPoint(line, position)` | `{ point, distance, chainage, fraction }`: the closest point on the line, how far it is, how far along the line, and the fraction of the line. |
| `network.geo.destination(from, bearing, distance)` | The position `distance` away from `from` on a bearing in degrees. |

`map.bounds` is the user's viewport at run start, so `network.findWithin(map.bounds)` scopes a script to what the user is looking at.

### 1.6 Topology and tracing

| Member | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `network.trace(start, { mode }?)` | The app's Trace tool, boundary mode: the pressure zone around `start` (an asset, a label, or a list of them). It grows through open links and stops at reservoirs and tanks (not included), pumps, closed links and every valve except TCVs. Returns `{ nodes, links, boundaryLinks }`. `mode` may only be `"allowed"` (the default); `"upstream"` and `"downstream"` need simulation results and throw. |
| `network.boundaryLinks(nodes)` | The rim of any set of nodes (objects or labels): every link with exactly one end inside, as `[{ link, inside, outside }]`. |
| `network.shortestPath(from, to, { weightBy }?)` | The cheapest path between two nodes (objects or labels): `{ nodes, links, totalLength }`, or `null` when they are not connected. `weightBy` is `"length"` (the default — pipe lengths, pumps and valves cost 0) or a function `(link) => number` returning a cost of at least 0. |
| `valve.targetNodeOptions()` | For a PRV, the nodes the asset panel offers as its remote set-point target (downstream of the valve); `[]` for any other kind. |

Boundary entries are `{ link, inside, outside }`, not links: for a PRV on the rim, `inside` is the zone end. Do not hand-roll a breadth-first search — `trace`, `boundaryLinks` and `shortestPath` cover it.

### 1.7 Network review and validation

These are the app's own checks — a script gets exactly what the Network Review panel and the Run button get. They run on the active network only (inactive assets are left out).

| Member | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `network.validate()` | The checks behind the dialog that opens when you press Run (see below). |
| `network.findOrphanAssets()` | The orphan check: nodes with no links, links missing an end, and pumps or valves with nothing else connected at either end — in the review panel's order (by type, then label). |
| `network.findSubnetworks()` | The connectivity check: every connected part of the network, largest first, as `[{ nodes, links, supplySourceCount, pipeCount, bounds }]`. A part with `supplySourceCount === 0` has no reservoir or tank. Parts of a single node are left out (they are orphans). |
| `network.findProximityAnomalies({ distance })` | The proximity check: nodes within `distance` (project length unit) of a pipe they are not connected to, nearest first, as `[{ node, pipe, distance, nearestPointOnPipe }]`. The review panel's default is 0.5 m or 1.5 ft. |
| `network.findCrossingPipes()` | The crossing check: pipes that cross on the map with no junction where they meet, as `[{ pipe1, pipe2, intersectionPoint }]` — the smaller pipe is `pipe1`. |

**`network.validate()`** returns `{ status, checks, counts, findings }`:
- `status` — `"ok"` (no findings: Run goes straight through), `"warning"` (only warnings) or `"error"` (at least one error). Run opens its review dialog for both `"warning"` and `"error"`.
- `checks` — `["orphanAssets", "connectivityTrace", "modelAttributesValidation"]`.
- `counts` — `{ findings, errors, warnings, assets }`.
- `findings` — orphan assets first, then one finding per area with no reservoir or tank, then the attribute rules, errors before warnings. Each is `{ check, code, severity, entityType, field, assets, details }`:
  - `code` — the app's stable rule id: `"asset.connected"`, `"subNetwork.supplySource.present"`, or an attribute rule such as `"pipe.diameter.present"`, `"node.elevation.present"`, `"pipe.material.inLibrary"`, `"customerPoint.connected"`.
  - `entityType` — what the rule is about (`"pipe"`, `"tank"`, `"customerPoint"`, …); `null` for the topology checks and for rules shared across types (`node.elevation.present` covers junctions and tanks — read each asset's `type`).
  - `field` — the property the rule judges, or `null`.
  - `assets` — everything that failed it (assets or customer points).
  - `details` — `{ nodes, links }` for an unsupplied area, else `null`.
- Orphan tanks and reservoirs are not findings: EPANET solves with them. `findOrphanAssets()` still lists them.

`findCrossingPipes()` and `findProximityAnomalies()` are informational — never a reason a run fails.

### 1.8 Export

| Member | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `network.toInp()` | The network as INP text, built the way File › Export INP builds it (coordinates, label ids, customer demands and water quality included), from the model the script reads. |

When the model needs **EPANET-LSX** — it has remote set-point PRVs or variable-speed pump controls — `toInp()` logs a console warning naming those assets. The file then carries a `[SCRIPT]` section that standard EPANET cannot run. Save it with `ui.attachFile(network.name + ".inp", network.toInp())`.

## 2. `selection` — the user's selection in, the script's out

| Member | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `selection.assets` | The selected assets. |
| `selection.customerPoints` | The selected customer points. |
| `selection.nodes`, `.links`, `.junctions`, `.reservoirs`, `.tanks`, `.pipes`, `.pumps`, `.valves` | The selected assets of that kind. |
| `selection.labels` | The labels of everything selected. |
| `selection.count`, `selection.isEmpty` | How many things are selected; whether nothing is. |
| `selection.set(targets)` | Replace the selection with an asset, a customer point or a list of them. |
| `selection.add(targets)` | Add to the selection. |
| `selection.clear()` | Select nothing. |

At run start the selection is the user's. After `set`, `add` or `clear`, the getters (and `asset.isSelected`) read the script's selection, and the map shows it when the script ends. `set`/`add` throw `selection.set expects assets or customer points from the network` for anything else.

When the user says "the selected pipes", start from `selection.pipes`, and throw a clear error when it is empty: `if (selection.pipes.length === 0) throw new Error("Select some pipes first")`.

## 3. `map` — the viewport

| Member | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `map.bounds` | The viewport at run start, `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]`, or `null`. |
| `map.center` | `[lng, lat]`, or `null`. |
| `map.zoom` | The zoom level, or `null`. |
| `map.zoomTo(target, { maxZoom }?)` | Zoom to assets, customer points or a bounding box when the script ends. The last call wins. |

## 4. `console` — output

| Member | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `console.log(...args)`, `console.warn(...args)`, `console.error(...args)` | A line in the run's console, streamed live. Assets and customer points print as their labels; objects print as JSON (with assets inside as labels). |
| `console.table(rows, columns?)` | A table. `rows` is an array of objects (or of plain values); `columns` picks and orders the keys. Asset cells print as labels. |

`JSON.stringify(asset)` gives `{}` — assets are getters, not data. Build plain objects of the fields you need (`{ pipe: p.label, diameter: p.diameter }`), or pass the asset to `console`/`ui.attachFile`, which print labels.

## 5. `ui` — progress and files

| Member | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `ui.progress(fraction, message?)` | Show progress between 0 and 1 in the run dialog. Calls closer than 50 ms apart with the same message are dropped, so calling it every iteration is fine. |
| `ui.attachFile(name, content)` | Offer a file for download when the script ends. `content` is a string, or an object/array written as indented JSON (assets inside become labels). The name is 1–128 characters; attaching the same name again replaces the file. |

Deliver tabular or geographic output as files — CSV, GeoJSON, JSON, INP — and keep `console.table` for at-a-glance summaries.

## 6. Errors and limits

- **An uncaught error stops the script.** The run dialog shows `name: message` and the script line it came from. Selection, zoom and attachments are not applied; console lines already printed stay.
- **API misuse throws early with a specific message**, for example `network.findNear expects { radius } as a number of at least 0, in the project length unit`, `network.customAttributes expects one of junction, reservoir, tank, pipe, pump, valve, customerPoint`, `map.zoomTo expects assets, customer points or a [minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat] box`, `network.trace found no asset labelled "X"`.
- **Cancellation:** the run dialog's Cancel stops the script immediately. There is no time limit.
- **Caps:** a console line keeps its first 10,000 characters; the run dialog keeps the last 1,000 console entries; `console.table` shows the first 1,000 rows and says how many it left out; a progress message keeps 200 characters.

## 7. Notes for AI agents

- Orient once: start the first script on an unfamiliar model with `console.log(network.stats)` and `console.log(network.units)`.
- Check `network.units` before hard-coding a threshold. A pipe diameter of 100 is 100 mm in one project and 100 in in another.
- Prefer `getNode`/`getLink` over `get`; never persist `uid`s; address assets by label.
- Everything is read-only. If the user asks to change the model, say so — do not write a script that assigns to asset fields.
- No `Date.now()`, `new Date()` or `Math.random()`: they throw in this sandbox.
- `JSON.stringify(asset)` is `{}`. Map assets to plain objects of the fields you need before serialising.
- Use the app's own checks instead of re-implementing them: `network.validate()`, `findOrphanAssets()`, `findSubnetworks()`, `findProximityAnomalies({ distance })`, `findCrossingPipes()`, `trace`, `boundaryLinks`, `shortestPath`.
- `network.validate()`'s `findings[0]` is the worst problem; `code` is stable; `assets` names what to fix.
- Read `pipe.appliedRoughness`, not `pipe.roughness`, for the value EPANET receives.
- Junction demand is `junction.demands` (categories with patterns) plus the demand of `junction.customerPoints`; `junction.baseDemand` is the categories only.
- Hand results back visually: `selection.set(...)` and `map.zoomTo(...)` for what to look at, `ui.attachFile` for data, `console.table` for a summary.
- When the user says "the selected …", start from `selection.*` and fail clearly when it is empty or the wrong type.

## 8. Worked examples

### Network overview

```js
console.log(`${network.name}: ${network.stats.junctions} junctions, ${network.stats.pipes} pipes`);
console.log(network.units);
const smallest = network.pipes
  .sort((a, b) => a.diameter - b.diameter)
  .slice(0, 10)
  .map((p) => ({ pipe: p, diameter: p.diameter, length: p.length }));
console.table(smallest);
```

### Select small pipes

```js
const maxDiameter = 100; // in network.units.diameter
const small = network.pipes.filter((p) => p.isActive && p.diameter <= maxDiameter);
console.log(`${small.length} of ${network.pipes.length} pipes ≤ ${maxDiameter} ${network.units.diameter}`);
selection.set(small);
map.zoomTo(small);
```

### Check the model will run

```js
const report = network.validate();
if (report.status === "ok") {
  console.log("Ready to run: no issues found");
} else {
  const { errors, warnings } = report.counts;
  console.warn(`${report.status}: ${errors} errors, ${warnings} warnings`);
  console.table(report.findings.map((f) => ({ severity: f.severity, code: f.code, assets: f.assets.length })));
  selection.set(report.findings[0].assets);
  map.zoomTo(report.findings[0].assets);
}
```

### Trace a pressure zone from the selection

```js
const start = selection.nodes[0];
if (!start) throw new Error("Select a node first");
const zone = network.trace(start);
console.log(`${zone.nodes.length} nodes, ${zone.links.length} links`);
console.table(zone.boundaryLinks.map(({ link, inside, outside }) => ({ link, type: link.type, inside, outside })));
const assets = [...zone.nodes, ...zone.links];
selection.set(assets);
map.zoomTo(assets);
```

### Export pipes in view as CSV

```js
const pipes = network.findWithin(map.bounds, { types: ["pipe"] });
const rows = ["label,diameter,length,material,appliedRoughness"];
for (const p of pipes) {
  rows.push([p.label, p.diameter, p.length, p.material ?? "", p.appliedRoughness ?? ""].join(","));
}
ui.attachFile("pipes-in-view.csv", rows.join("\n"));
console.log(`${pipes.length} pipes in view`);
```

### Export the network as INP

```js
const name = `${network.name}.inp`;
ui.attachFile(name, network.toInp());
console.log(`Exported ${network.nodes.length} nodes and ${network.links.length} links to ${name}`);
```
